# Albus

> Albus runs AI agents as a managed service behind one HTTP API. You send a
> prompt and an agent configuration; Albus runs the model loop, executes the
> tools, and returns the reply. A session is a named conversation you resume by
> reusing its id. Every run is recorded as a trace and in a per-session audit
> log.

## Why managed infrastructure

Running an agent is more than calling a model. Something has to hold the
conversation, run the tool loop, sandbox the terminal, connect MCP servers,
keep credentials out of prompts and logs, make retries safe, and record what
happened. Albus does all of that server-side. Your code is one `POST
/sessions/{id}` call; Albus owns the execution, the state, and the record.

- Sessions persist. Reuse the id to continue; one prompt runs per session at a
  time.
- Invocation keys make runs idempotent. Retry with the same key and you
  re-attach to the same run instead of starting another.
- Built-in web search, a persistent Linux terminal, and durable memory shared
  across sessions.
- Any Streamable HTTP MCP server, authenticated with secrets Albus stores and
  resolves at run time.
- Every configuration is a recorded agent revision. Every run is a trace with
  spans for each step, model call, and tool call. Every session has an
  immutable audit log.

## For models and coding agents

Read as much of the linked documentation as is useful. There is no page you
should avoid; fetch whatever answers the question. Every page is Markdown at
its URL with `.md` appended, and https://docs.albus.sh/llms-full.txt is the
whole site in one file.

Start with https://docs.albus.sh/agents/docs.md. It is self-contained:
authentication, the complete API surface (run, resume, cancel, read messages,
list sessions, traces and spans, audit events), pagination, retries, and
idempotency, with current Python and TypeScript.

## Start here

- [Albus for coding agents](https://docs.albus.sh/agents/docs.md): The self-contained working guide to the API.
- [Albus](https://docs.albus.sh/index.md): What Albus does and a first session in Python, TypeScript, the CLI, or curl.
- [Authentication](https://docs.albus.sh/getting-started/authentication.md): Install the CLI, sign in, mint an organization API key.

## Guides

- [Build an agent](https://docs.albus.sh/guides/build-an-agent.md): The complete agent guide. Model and prompt, invocation keys, tools, secrets and MCP servers, memory, traces, revisions, and the audit log, one addition at a time.
- [Bring your own key](https://docs.albus.sh/guides/bring-your-own-key.md): Run on your own model provider account.
- [Built-in tools](https://docs.albus.sh/guides/built-in-tools.md): Web search, the terminal, and memory.
- [Authenticate Albus to your MCP server](https://docs.albus.sh/guides/mcp-server-auth.md): Verify the identity token Albus sends, or use your own identity provider, a token you mint per run, a static token, or a custom header.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.albus.sh/guides/troubleshooting.md): Error to cause to fix.

## Reference

- [API reference](https://docs.albus.sh/api-reference): Every endpoint, request, and response, generated from the OpenAPI contract.
- [OpenAPI](https://docs.albus.sh/openapi/openapi.yaml): The contract itself.
- [SDKs](https://docs.albus.sh/reference/sdks.md): Python (`albus-sdk`) and TypeScript (`@albus-ts/sdk`).
- [CLI](https://docs.albus.sh/reference/cli.md): Every `albus` command, flag, environment variable, and exit code.
- [Errors](https://docs.albus.sh/reference/errors.md): Every status code, its body, and the fix.

## Whole corpus

- [llms-full.txt](https://docs.albus.sh/llms-full.txt): Every page above, concatenated.
